record.paper_title: Orthogonality Types in Normed Linear Spaces
record.original_question: For fixed real parameters a and b, with the two-parameter Carlsson relation x ⊥_{a,b} y defined by ∥x - y∥^2 + ∥a x - b y∥^2 = ∥x - b y∥^2 + ∥y - a x∥^2, does symmetry alone force X to be an inner product space? Here symmetry means that x ⊥_{a,b} y implies y ⊥_{a,b} x for all vectors x and y; the known stronger hypothesis was symmetry plus additivity.

evidence.quote: Question 4.9.2 Does symmetry alone imply the same result?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X, \|\cdot\|)$ be a real normed linear space, and fix real parameters $a, b$. Define the Carlsson two-parameter orthogonality relation $\perp_{a,b}$ on $X$ by
$$x \perp_{a,b} y \iff \|x - y\|^2 + \|ax - by\|^2 = \|x - by\|^2 + \|y - ax\|^2.$$
Say that $\perp_{a,b}$ is symmetric on $X$ if for all $x, y \in X$, $x \perp_{a,b} y$ implies $y \perp_{a,b} x$.

It is known that if $\perp_{a,b}$ is both symmetric and additive (i.e., $x \perp_{a,b} y$ and $x \perp_{a,b} z$ imply $x \perp_{a,b} (y+z)$) on $X$, and the parameters satisfy the relevant nondegeneracy conditions, then the norm on $X$ is induced by an inner product.

Question: Does the symmetry of $\perp_{a,b}$ alone (without assuming additivity) force the norm on $X$ to be induced by an inner product?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turned up related work on Carlsson-type orthogonality and inner-product-space characterizations (e.g., via HH-norms, unitary Carlsson-type orthogonalities), but no result was found that resolves whether symmetry alone of the general two-parameter Carlsson orthogonality $\perp_{a,b}$ characterizes inner product spaces. The status appears to remain open or undetermined in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of Inner Product Spaces by Unitary Carlsson-type orthogonality
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizations via symmetric unitary Carlsson-type orthogonality are studied, building on Carlsson's framework.
status_evidence.claim: Existing characterizations typically require additional hypotheses (such as homogeneity or specific norms) beyond symmetry alone.

status_evidence.title: On Uniqueness of New Orthogonality via 2-HH Norm in Normed Linear Space
status_evidence.snippet: A Carlsson-type orthogonality via the 2-HH norm is introduced and characterizations of inner product spaces are derived under added structural assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Known characterizations rely on hypotheses stronger than mere symmetry of the Carlsson relation.
